$comment: Implementation status for the Tool Mode specifications. Consumed by scripts/gen-traceability.mjs. Anything absent here is reported as NOT_RUN. Update this file as work lands; never edit TRACEABILITY.md by hand.

notes.MCP-01: VERIFIED BLOCKER: the latest published @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (1.32.1) declares LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2025-11-25 and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS=[2025-11-25,2025-06-18,2025-03-26,2024-11-05,2024-10-07]. It does NOT support 2026-07-28. That revision IS published upstream (schema/2026-07-28/ and a 2026-07-28 git tag exist in modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol), so MCP-01's 'separately reviewed, schema-conformant adaptation' clause is the route that must be taken: the wire layer has to be implemented against the official schema rather than delegated to the SDK.
notes.DEC-01: VERIFIED BLOCKER: the npm package `laya-ts` named by DEC-02 does not exist (registry returns 404). No published Node entry point for Laya was found on npm. Milestone D's Laya default cannot be qualified until a real distribution channel is identified; BASE-14 forbids substituting an unrelated model silently.
notes.DEC-02: BLOCKED on the same missing `laya-ts` package. DEC-02 additionally requires a maintainer-run ONNX export in controlled CI plus numerical-parity evidence, which cannot be executed here without the source checkpoint and Python toolchain.
notes.NDL-01: PARTIAL EVIDENCE: cactus-compute/needle exists on GitHub (13,894 stars; 'automation foundation model for tiny devices') and as a Hugging Face repo. No node-named npm distribution for Needle 3 was found (@cactus-compute/needle and needle-ai both 404; `cactus-needle@0.3.0` exists but is unverified against NDL-01's requirements). The NDL-01 runtime strategy is therefore unqualified.
notes.MODEL-01: PARTIAL EVIDENCE: google/embeddinggemma-2 exists on Hugging Face (124,930 downloads, ungated); google/embeddinggemma-300m exists but is gated=manual, which would require the operator to accept terms before download. sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 are both present and ungated, matching BASE-12's preserved 384-dimensional space.
notes.AT-01: NOT_RUN: requires a clean compatible DSH installation and a built tarball install. The current package is published and installable (verified for @try-works/dsh-model-as-tool@0.1.1), but the Tool Mode bundle does not exist yet.
notes.AT-04: NOT_RUN and currently unreachable: requires a genuine 2026-07-28 reference client. The published SDK cannot speak that revision, so the client side must come from the schema-conformant adaptation described under MCP-01.

BASE-01.evidence: Catalog, adapters, skills, persistence and platform checks preserved; the plugin was extended in place across commits fcb79ea..2e27e2a rather than recreated.

BASE-02.evidence: Tool identity is now independent of model identity: a catalog `contract` binding decides the tool name, the host registers ONE tool per contract, and a two-implementation catalog test proves two models yield one `lang_detect`. Adapter factories are now keyed on the npm PACKAGE rather than the model id, because keying on the id was itself a model-name switch that made a second conforming implementation unservable. Provider override is host config with documented fallback. Remaining: the merge is proven with test fixtures, not with two distinct real models.

BASE-03.evidence: `stt_transcribe` is now the canonical registered name and `transcribe_audio` is an opt-in alias (`legacyAliases`, default false) so it stays out of the default catalog. Tests assert the alias is absent by default, appears only when enabled, and keeps its own argument shape (`audio_path`) rather than being reinterpreted as the canonical contract's (`audio.path`). Remaining: not exercised against a real recording.

BASE-04.evidence: Explicit requiredness comes from the contract schema required array; parameter-order inference is gone from the contract path. Real per-tool output schemas are enforced by Ajv on every result. DSH cannot advertise every JSON-Schema keyword, so the projection reports what it omits and argument validation enforces it against the untouched contract (tested: minLength is reported as runtime-enforced and still rejects a short value). Remaining: the legacy per-model registrar path still infers requiredness from parameter order.

MODEL-01.evidence: Availability verified only: google/embeddinggemma-2 exists on Hugging Face ungated (124,930 downloads). No adapter, packaging or modality test exists yet.

DECL-01.evidence: Contracts are authored once with stable name, identity, version, input/output schema, semantics, limits and unsupported cases; DSH parameter projection is generated from that one source. MCP projection and Code Mode type generation are not implemented.

DECL-02.evidence: The two standard contracts publish real requiredness, nesting, nullability and units, and validation REFUSES an open-object output or a missing envelope (tested). Covers 2 of the release tool set; the remaining contracts do not exist.

DECL-03.evidence: ToolMeta is defined once and now STAMPED BY THE HOST on every contract-registered call: extension/version/receipt come from host state and the implementation cannot forge them. Tests assert the envelope, the implementation id that actually ran, distinct receipts per call, and that an adapter cannot override the host identity. Remaining: host stamping covers contract-registered tools only.

DECL-04.evidence: Contracts declare scoreKind/calibrated, and a fabricated `confidence` field is refused by output validation (tested). Not yet enforced across the whole tool surface.

TOOL-01.evidence: The stt.transcribe contract declares transcription-not-translation, seconds from start-of-audio, empty-is-valid, partial coverage via coverage.complete, error-on-unsupported-timestamp, and the admitted 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV limits. No implementation is bound and no real audio has been transcribed through it.

TOOL-03.evidence: The text.language_detect contract preserves ambiguity (candidates + tooCloseToCall), declares scoreKind, and states that it is written-text-only and not evidence about spoken audio. Not yet bound to an implementation through the contract.

DEC-01.evidence: No distribution channel: npm `laya-ts` returns 404 and no published Node entry point for Laya was found. Needs an operator decision (see note).

DEC-02.evidence: Same missing `laya-ts` entry point, plus DEC-02 requires a maintainer-run ONNX export in CI with numerical-parity evidence, which needs the source checkpoint and a Python toolchain.

NDL-01.evidence: Needle exists upstream (github.com/cactus-compute/needle, HF cactus-compute/needle) but no verified Node/WASM distribution for Needle 3 was found; the runtime strategy is unqualified.

BASE-05.evidence: The host now constructs an InvocationAuthority from an operator-built grant and passes it to every adapter, so a request cannot supply or widen it. It carries grantId, caller kind, limits, recording policy and a resolvePath bound to the approved roots; a test asserts the object exposes no mutable roots list. SEC-03 tool grants and SEC-10 destination grants are enforced before inference. Remaining: filesystem access is wired into the Voz path tool but not every adapter, and the harness-executor/capability fields of SEC-03 do not exist yet.

SEC-03.evidence: createGrant models allowedTools, approvedRoots, remoteDestinations, hostedCode, recordingPolicy and limits; authorizeTool/authorizeDestination refuse before any model work. Defaults are conservative (no hosted code, no recording, no roots, so it fails closed). Remaining: per-application independently revocable credentials (SEC-01) and harness-executor profiles are not implemented, and the interactive grant covers the standard tools rather than being created per client.

SEC-06.evidence: authorizePath resolves drive letters, separators, Unicode, junctions and symlinks via realpathSync.native, then checks containment on a separator boundary; it refuses relative paths, UNC and Windows device paths, NUL bytes, missing paths and anything outside every root, and returns the CANONICAL path so the caller opens what was authorized rather than re-resolving it (closing the check-then-open race). Tested against real directories and real Windows junctions, including Unicode and space-containing valid paths, a sibling whose name shares a prefix, traversal, and links that stay inside. 1 of 24 cases skipped where the platform forbids file symlinks without elevation; the equivalent junction case covers that escape.

SEC-10.evidence: authorizeDestination refuses an unauthorized remote destination, and the grant exposes no silent local-to-remote fallback path. Remaining: the hosted-code and harness-executor edges of the rule are not implemented.

EXT-13.evidence: discoverExtension reads package.json and the manifest as BOUNDED data (256 KB / 512 KB limits) and never imports the entry: the test fixture writes an entry that throws on import, and reaching the assertions proves it never ran. It enforces name, version, type:module, an explicit exports map, the toolMode.manifest field, containment of the manifest path, and rejects malformed or oversized JSON as INVALID_EXTENSION. Remaining: quarantine fetch, archive inspection and the install/activate lifecycle are not implemented.

EXT-14.evidence: extension-manifest-1.1.0.schema.json ships with the SDK and is enforced at runtime via Ajv 2020-12. Beyond the schema it checks exact id/version agreement with the package, unique local ids per contribution kind, duplicate caller-facing tool NAMES reported as TOOL_NAME_CONFLICT, referenced files that must exist, paths that must not escape the package, and unknown REQUIRED features blocking activation as INCOMPATIBLE_PROTOCOL. Unknown top-level fields are rejected while the x- vendor namespace is admitted. Remaining: asset-lock validation (EXT-15) and keyed digests.

EXT-16.evidence: A 1.0 manifest is normalized to module execution as a VIEW, leaving the input object untouched so the recorded digest still describes the installed bytes; the lift provenance is attached after validation rather than smuggled past the closed schema. Protocol 1.1.0, runtime API major 1, and the five separate identities are documented in code. Remaining: minor-version conformance tests and the contract/recipe/model revision separation are not implemented end to end.

EXT-17.evidence: The SDK now defines and exports the complete public runtime API: ToolModeExtensionV1, ExtensionContextV1, ExtensionInstanceV1, ModelProviderV1, ProviderInspectionV1, PreparedAssetMapV1, InvocationContextV1, JsonObject/JsonValue, the DisposeReason vocabulary, defineExtension() which rejects a wrong apiVersion at the declaration site, and the reserved-meta guard. Loading is implemented in load.ts: the entry is resolved from the package own exports map rather than a convention, the shape is validated BEFORE create() runs, and a missing dispose() is refused because a host with no way to release an instance could never fully stop it. Remaining: the declarative interpreter, the conformance helpers, and the reference test host with a fake harness broker are not implemented, and the SDK is not published to npm.

EXT-25.evidence: The six dimensions are modelled separately and now PERSIST: a profile state file round-trips installation, desired and observed activation, per-deployment readiness, per-profile tool selection with the selected implementation, and export authorization independently, with profiles kept apart. A corrupt or oversized file, or one malformed entry, invalidates the whole file rather than dropping just the bad part, because a file that is demonstrably untrustworthy must not activate anything. Remaining: activation does not yet write these states, so persistence is exercised by tests rather than by a lifecycle operation.

EXT-34.evidence: All 15 published codes exist with the operation, safe recovery advice and a retryable flag DERIVED from the code so a permission refusal cannot be mistaken for a transient fault. Recovery text is passed through a sanitiser that strips credential- and path-shaped spans. Remaining: the codes are not yet raised by install/activate/uninstall, which do not exist.

EXT-07.evidence: stagedInstall returns `activation: "inactive"` as an explicit field so a caller cannot mistake a successful install for a usable tool, and it imports nothing: the test fixture ships an entry that THROWS on import, so reaching the assertions proves installation never executed it. No inference, no warming, no tool or skill publication. Remaining: no inventory and no activation path, so the state an install produces is not yet persisted or readable.

EXT-08.evidence: The ordered pipeline runs and now RECORDS its result: fetch into a unique quarantine directory -> verify SHA-512 -> list entries -> validate the entry list -> extract -> discover as data -> promote by atomic rename -> record in the store lock -> remove quarantine on every path. Recording happens AFTER the bytes are in place, because a lock entry naming a directory that does not exist would make verification report a missing installation as a changed one. Remaining: dependency resolution and locking, the permission/licence/platform preview, and operator approval are not implemented.

EXT-11.evidence: Entry-list validation refuses traversal, absolute paths, drive letters, UNC, backslashes, NUL bytes, Windows reserved device names, segments ending in a dot or space, duplicates, Windows case collisions, symlinks and hardlinks, plus entry-count, per-entry, total-byte and expansion-ratio bounds. Tested against REAL zip archives built at the byte level, because adm-zip sanitizes entry names on write and therefore cannot produce the hostile archives these defenses exist to refuse; a raw ZIP writer in the test suite supplies the bytes. The extractor re-asserts confinement at the write, so a bypassed validator still cannot escape. Remaining: fetch time limits are passed through but not enforced by the SDK, which owns no network stack.

EXT-33.evidence: The store now RECORDS what it installs: an operator-owned extensions.lock.json holds complete resolved source/identity records (identity, version, install path, archive digest, CONTENT digest, source, timestamp), so identity survives restart and a package edited on disk after installation is detected before activation rather than trusted. Version-keyed layout keeps two versions side by side. Corrupted state FAILS CLOSED: a lock or profile file that cannot be trusted yields NO records and a diagnostic, never a fallback to "everything installed is active", and a lock that could not be read is refused as an append target rather than silently overwritten. All writes are atomic (temp plus rename) and a failed write throws instead of reporting success. Remaining: per-install dependency locks and transaction records are not implemented, and cleanup-pending tombstones do not exist.

EXT-26.evidence: Activation verifies the installed bytes and locks BEFORE publishing anything (a package edited after installation is refused as INTEGRITY_MISMATCH with nothing published), persists intended-active before publication so a crash leaves a record rather than a silent no-op, publishes every required contribution through an injected registrar, and commits the catalog generation ONLY once all of them were accepted. A failed registration rolls back narrowly: only the handles this activation published are withdrawn, the generation does not advance, and a healthy extension stays active AND callable - tested with one good and one failing package in the same profile. Readiness is assessed rather than assumed: merely unprepared assets activate with needs-preparation diagnostics as EXT-26 requires, while a FAILED deployment refuses activation because it will not become ready by waiting. Remaining: no managed worker is started and the public entry/API is not validated, because there is no worker runtime; provider handles are not created.

EXT-27.evidence: Deactivation persists inactive intent BEFORE withdrawing anything, verified by reading a fresh store from inside the withdrawal callback so the assertion is about the durable file rather than an in-memory view; if the process died mid-deactivation a restart would read "off" rather than resurrect the package. Contributions are withdrawn, and a withdrawal that fails does NOT produce a full-stop claim: the result reports fullyStopped false with the exact cleanup failure and the state becomes quarantined while desired activation stays inactive. A deactivated extension is not admitted even when its individual tool remains enabled, which is the orthogonal-state case a single boolean would collapse. Remaining: active calls are not cancelled, disposal hooks are not called, no grace period is joined, and no owned process is terminated, because there is no worker runtime; queued calls and cached Code Mode bindings do not exist.

EXT-28.evidence: Uninstalling an active package returns EXTENSION_IN_USE unless deactivation is explicitly requested, and with it the deactivation sequence runs first. Removal clears the installation record but RETAINS the disabled tombstone, so nothing silently resurrects the package. Removing the record does not delete the installed bytes, deliberately: deletion has its own failure modes (EXT-29) and conflating the two would make a failed deletion look like a failed uninstall. Remaining: no preview of affected profiles/tools is produced, private resolved dependencies are not deleted, credential references and executable-content approvals are not revoked, and BUILTIN_PROTECTED is not yet reachable because no built-in is identified as such.

EXT-04.evidence: Every extension is deactivatable through the same path, a built-in being a first-party package rather than an exception. Individual tools toggle independently of activation: disabling one tool leaves the package active and its other tools callable, and toggling an unknown tool is refused rather than ignored. Uninstall is implemented for third-party packages with the EXTENSION_IN_USE gate. Remaining: BUILTIN_PROTECTED is unreachable because nothing is marked built-in yet, and asset purging does not exist.

BASE-09.evidence: The private built-in adapter path is gone for Tongue: the host no longer contains an adapter for it, the code moved to the independently versioned package @try-works/extension-desert-ant-tongue, and the host reaches it only by importing the package PUBLIC ./tool-mode entry and calling create()/createProvider(). The binding from a catalog model to its package is DATA (a `provider` field, validated at catalog load), not a switch on the model name, so a first-party and a third-party package take the identical route. ADAPTER_FACTORIES in the host is now empty and documented as needing to stay so. Remaining: Voz is still a host-resident adapter held in adapters/voz.ts and reached only from a single call site; it must become @try-works/extension-desert-ant-voz. The remaining deviation is confined to one function so its removal deletes code rather than editing a list that looks legitimate.

EXT-02.evidence: The first extracted extension imports ONLY @try-works/tool-mode-extension-sdk (its runtime dependency) and never host internals, which is what makes it buildable by an author who has not installed the host. The SDK runs the extension through the published interfaces and its own tests exercise it the same way a host does. Remaining: nothing enforces the prohibition mechanically, so a future extension could still reach for a host path; a lint or packaging check would be needed to make it a gate rather than a convention.

EXT-18.evidence: All five named context contracts exist with the required semantics documented: ExtensionContextV1 carries host-issued identity, private storage, a bounded logger and a teardown signal, and deliberately NO DSH ctx, registry mutation, global credentials or unfiltered environment; ProviderInspectionV1 reports readiness/features/missing/runtimeVersion and inspection is implemented to read only approved local state (a test asserts it reports unprepared before a load rather than claiming ready); PreparedAssetMapV1 and InvocationContextV1 carry verified handles and call-scoped grants with no caller-supplied authority. Remaining: the asset map is a type without a host implementation, and the file/network broker operations are typed but have no enforcing host behind them.

EXT-19.evidence: Import and create() are lightweight and tested: the extension declares no assets because Tongue bundles its weights, module import performs no work, and a test asserts createProvider returns a handle in well under a second rather than parsing the weight file, with inspect() reporting unprepared until load() is called. Disposal is idempotent and the host disposes providers per model and instances per extension. Remaining: there is no pooling, no concurrency admission, and unload() is only a cache drop because no provider holds a process-level resource yet.

AT-13.evidence: Windows traversal, absolute-path escape, junction escape, device/UNC paths and unauthorized roots are all refused, with Unicode and space-containing valid paths admitted (authority.test.ts, real filesystem). Remaining: the artifact/receipt identifier half of the test, which needs a receipt store that does not exist yet.

AT-01.evidence: Requires a clean compatible DSH installation and a built tarball of the Tool Mode bundle. The packages build and install individually, but the bundle does not exist yet.

AT-18.evidence: The durable-write half is satisfied for the extension store: a write that fails throws rather than reporting success, all writes go through a temporary file and a rename, and no temporary file survives. Corrupted state fails closed with a diagnostic rather than enabling every installed package. Remaining: the migration half (existing enable/disable choices surviving an upgrade) is not exercised, because the extension store has no prior format to migrate from.
